title: SMB1001, short of the catalogue
interpretation_rule: Detailed controls are intentionally empty. The public architecture may be paraphrased. Control text, tier rules and certification logic stay out until an authorised SMB1001:2026 copy is supplied and the rights for derivative mapping, PDF publication, web presentation and MCP output are confirmed.
overall_conclusion: SMB1001:2026 is Dynamic Standards International’s five-level cybersecurity certification for small and medium-sized businesses. This briefing records the public architecture only. Detailed controls remain empty because the standard licence restricts external publication and requires prior written permission for derivative works.

levels.label: Level 1
levels.public_summary: Basic preventive controls, illustrated on the public page by firewalls and antivirus software.

levels.label: Level 2
levels.public_summary: More advanced preventive measures against more sophisticated threats.

levels.label: Level 3
levels.public_summary: Holistic risk management across people, processes and technology.

levels.label: Levels 4 and 5
levels.public_summary: More complex governance: formal rules and policies, and risk-management practice. The public page states these two levels together.

focus_areas.name: Technology Management
focus_areas.public_summary: Oversight of hardware, software and networks, including updates, vulnerability patching and security configuration.

native_modules.how: Candidate only, because the public Level 1 line mentions antivirus. Not classified as the control.
native_modules.boundary: Platform coverage, exceptions and operating effectiveness are not assessed.

native_modules.how: Candidate only, because the public focus area mentions patching. Not classified as the control.
native_modules.boundary: Scan cadence, catalogue and deployment evidence are not assessed.

native_modules.how: Candidate only, for asset visibility against the public technology-estate sentence.
native_modules.boundary: A complete inventory is not evidenced.

native_modules.how: Candidate only, for automated updates. Not classified as the control.
native_modules.boundary: Host and software scope are not assessed against a quoted requirement.

native_modules.how: Candidate only, for telemetry after configuration or prevention fails.
native_modules.boundary: Telemetry is not itself the configuration.

ecosystem_controls.how: The public sentence gives upkeep of the technology estate to the business. A sensor does not approve exceptions.
Assets outside a supported sensor stay outside any future native claim.
Generative tools are software under the public description. No AI-security module is in the research queue.

gaps_and_residual.gap: The licensed control text is not available.
gaps_and_residual.residual: No technology-management control is classified, and no coverage claim is made.

gaps_and_residual.gap: The public sentence is an estate, not an endpoint.
gaps_and_residual.residual: Firmware, network devices, unsupported platforms and AI tooling stay with the organisation.

focus_areas.name: Access Management
focus_areas.public_summary: Access limited to authorised people, including password policy, multi-factor authentication and monitoring of user activity.

native_modules.how: Candidate only, for identity risk and activity monitoring. Not classified as the control.
native_modules.boundary: Directory scope and conditional-access coverage are not assessed.

native_modules.how: Candidate only, for phishing-resistant authentication on supported flows.
native_modules.boundary: Which authentication paths exist is not assessed.

ecosystem_controls.how: Password policy, account lifecycle, recovery and the authoritative directory stay with the identity provider.

ecosystem_controls.component: Business owner of AI tool access
ecosystem_controls.how: Who may use a model, and with what data, is an access decision the public sentence does not assign to a sensor.

gaps_and_residual.gap: The licensed control text is not available.
Password policy does not govern prompts.
gaps_and_residual.residual: Control of model credentials, prompt content and shadow AI stays with the organisation.

focus_areas.name: Backup and Recovery
focus_areas.public_summary: Backups of critical data and a recovery plan that can restore systems after an incident and limit downtime and data loss.

native_modules.how: Candidate only, for detection of destructive activity around copies. Not a backup.
native_modules.boundary: Detection does not create a copy or run a restore.

native_modules.how: Candidate only, for evidence that an incident touched recovery systems.
native_modules.boundary: A log is not a restoration test.

ecosystem_controls.how: Copies, immutability, isolation, retention and restoration testing sit with the backup owner.
What counts as critical data, including model artefacts if the business holds them, is an organisational decision.

gaps_and_residual.gap: The licensed control text is not available.

gaps_and_residual.residual: A Falcon detection cannot stand in for a tested restore.

focus_areas.name: Policies, Plans and Procedures
focus_areas.public_summary: Cybersecurity policies, procedures and contingency plans, including how the organisation responds to incidents and protects sensitive information.

native_modules.how: Candidate only, for workflow and evidence once an incident process already exists.
native_modules.boundary: A feed does not write the policy or approve an exception.
An investigation record is not a contingency plan.

ecosystem_controls.how: Policies, plans, supplier rules and exception registers stay with the organisation.
An AI-use rule, where the business needs one, is not evidenced by a detection feed.

gaps_and_residual.gap: The licensed control text is not available.
gaps_and_residual.residual: Tier names, control counts and any AI-use policy in commentary are not adopted as requirements.

gaps_and_residual.gap: A policy is not a technical control.
gaps_and_residual.residual: Prompt-injection defence and the rest of the OWASP GenAI list stay an organisational design job.

focus_areas.name: Education and Training
focus_areas.public_summary: Ongoing training so staff know current threats and sound practice, with human error treated as a cause of incidents.

native_modules.how: Threat context can inform training. No awareness module was named for classification.
native_modules.boundary: Content, simulations and behaviour measurement are not a Falcon function in this assessment.

ecosystem_controls.how: The curriculum, the exercises and the measure of behaviour stay with the organisation.

gaps_and_residual.gap: The licensed control text is not available.
Current threats now include generative-AI tradecraft.
gaps_and_residual.residual: Training that stops at a generic phishing poster does not discharge the public sentence. That judgement is not an SMB1001 score.

assessment_scale.native_direct: CrowdStrike authoritatively performs a material part of the requirement.
assessment_scale.native_direct_bounded: CrowdStrike directly performs part of the requirement only for documented platforms, workloads, sources or flows.
assessment_scale.native_supporting: CrowdStrike supplies prevention, discovery, prioritisation, detection, response or evidence but does not own the required control.
assessment_scale.ecosystem: Another technology, platform control or organisational process is required.
assessment_scale.gap: No sufficient native capability is evidenced, or the requirement remains organisational.
assessment_scale.not_assessed: The licensed requirement, or the evidence needed to classify coverage, is not yet available. Every row in this briefing uses this class.

limitations: No authorised copy of the licensed standard was supplied.
No evidence of rights to publish a derivative control mapping was supplied.
Control identifiers, tier rules, attestation and certification evidence are absent on purpose.
Candidate CrowdStrike modules are research hypotheses, not assessed mappings.

The framework page, as recorded on 22 September 2026, advertises a separate commercial-use option for platforms and service delivery. That agreement was not supplied, and the sentence was not repeated in the page payload re-read for this briefing.
The next step is an authorised SMB1001:2026 copy and confirmation covering derivative mapping, PDF publication, web presentation and MCP output.
No customer entitlement, deployment, configuration or operating effectiveness was assessed.

The public page re-read on 22 September 2026 confirmed the level prose, the five focus areas and the licence terms. It did not contain the recorded 93-page count, the 1 September 2025 date, or the six FAQ example sentences.
A separate 2027 edition is not substituted for the 2026 baseline. The public page read here is the 2026 standard.
Wavestone’s AI figures are a slice of more than 20 large organisations. They are not the 200-organisation maturity average, and they are not an SMB sample.
CrowdStrike sells Falcon. The threat figures are vendor telemetry.
This briefing is not legal advice on the DSI licence.
